title: Microsoft Purview Insider Risk Management: built-in filter for temporary file noise on endpoints
summary: The briefing accurately reports the roadmap's planned filtering and target dates, and distinguishes existing exclusions from the undocumented new filter. The existing exclusions route is correct but stops early; the keyword entry route should name its final field.

claims.claim: Microsoft plans built-in IRM filtering for well-known temporary file name patterns.
claims.quote: This feature introduces built-in filtering for well-known temporary file name patterns

claims.claim: Opening files in Windows can cause the operating system to create, rename and delete temporary files.
claims.quote: When files are opened in Windows, the operating system, and applications (for example, Microsoft Office and browsers) can create, rename, and delete temporary files as part of normal behavior.

claims.claim: Applications such as Microsoft Office and browsers can create, rename and delete temporary files during normal Windows file use.
claims.quote: When files are opened in Windows, the operating system, and applications (for example, Microsoft Office and browsers) can create, rename, and delete temporary files as part of normal behavior.

claims.claim: The Endpoint client audits these temporary file operations.
claims.quote: The Endpoint client audits these activities

claims.claim: These audited temporary file operations produce high-volume, low-signal noise for IRM customers.
claims.quote: resulting in high-volume, low-signal events that appear as “noise” for Insider Risk Management (IRM) customers.

claims.claim: Existing global exclusions do not easily capture some temporary file naming patterns without over-excluding.
claims.quote: some temporary file naming patterns are not easily captured with the current exclusions, leaving customers without a practical way to reduce noise without over-excluding.

claims.claim: Global exclusions is reached in Microsoft Purview portal at Settings > Insider Risk Management > Insider risk settings > Global exclusions.
claims.quote: Select Settings in the upper-right corner of the page, then select Insider Risk Management to go to the Insider Risk Management settings. Under Insider risk settings, select Global exclusions.
claims.fix: The route reaches the correct page but stops before choosing an exclusion. Retain it and give the complete routes in the note: 'Settings > Insider Risk Management > Insider risk settings > Global exclusions > Type > File paths > Individual file paths > Add file paths to exclude'; 'Settings > Insider Risk Management > Insider risk settings > Global exclusions > Type > File types > Individual file types > Add file type'; 'Settings > Insider Risk Management > Insider risk settings > Global exclusions > Type > Keywords > Individual keywords > Exclude these keywords'. Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/insider-risk-management-settings-global-exclusions.

claims.where: controls[0].governs; Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance controls
claims.claim: Existing Global exclusions can exclude file types, keywords and file paths from IRM policy scoring to tune noise.
claims.quote: Use the Global exclusions setting in Microsoft Purview Insider Risk Management to exclude items from being scored by Insider Risk Management policies.

claims.claim: Global exclusions has tenant-wide scope over IRM policies.
claims.quote: Insider Risk Management settings apply to all Insider Risk Management policies, regardless of the template you choose when creating a policy.

claims.claim: Global exclusions includes a default file path exclusion for \Users\*\AppData\Local\Temp.
claims.quote: By default, the system automatically excludes several file paths from generating policy alerts. The default file path exclusions are: \Users\*\AppData; \Users\*\AppData\Local; \Users\*\AppData\Roaming; \Users\*\AppData\Local\Temp

claims.claim: Administrators can cancel default file path exclusion selections to enable risk scoring in those locations.
claims.quote: If needed, you can cancel the selection for these default file path exclusions to enable risk scoring for activities in these locations.

claims.claim: An event excluded through existing global exclusions is included in a sequence when it is part of the sequence due to an obfuscation activity.
claims.quote: if an event that's excluded from risk scoring is part of a sequence due to an obfuscation activity, the event is included in the sequence since it might be interesting in the context of the sequence.
